question: When following a motorcycle, how much following distance should you allow on dry pavement?
options: a:Allow at least two seconds of following distance.,b:Allow at least two car lengths.,c:Allow at least four seconds of following distance.
note: On dry pavement allow at least four seconds of following distance behind a motorcycle to give ample reaction and braking time.

question: When are you NOT required to stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?
options: a:If you are driving on the opposite side of a divided highway.,b:If you are behind the bus.,c:If you see no children present.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway.

question: Even small amounts of alcohol can do what to a driver?
options: a:Improve driving confidence without affecting skill.,b:Have no noticeable effect until exceeding the legal limit.,c:Reduce concentration
note: Even modest alcohol consumption impairs mental and physical skills needed for safe driving.

question: When is it legal to cross solid yellow centerlines?
options: a:To make a turn.,b:At any time.,c:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; crossing is permitted for making turns or as directed by signs.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the best reaction?
options: a:Pull alongside and confront the driver.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely rather than reacting aggressively.,c:Flash your high beams repeatedly to scare them.
note: Avoid road rage by not taking it personally; maintain safety and continue driving calmly.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are only found in construction zones.,b:Provide information for drivers.,c:Are usually not important.
note: Pavement markings convey information to drivers about lane positioning, passing zones, and upcoming conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:After you begin the lane change.,b:Only if another driver is following you closely.,c:Signal early enough before changing lanes to warn others.
note: Signal in advance of your lane change so other drivers are aware of your intention to pass.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the roadway after a stop, you must:
options: a:Yield and allow it to reenter.,b:Move to the left lane.,c:Honk to let the driver know you are there.
note: You must yield—by slowing, stopping, or changing lanes when safe—to allow buses to re-enter traffic after loading or unloading.

question: When are you allowed to go around a lowered or closing railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:When the lights have stopped flashing.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Never attempt to go around a lowered gate or ignored flashing signals; do not cross until it is safe and legal to do so.

question: How should you respond when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside?
options: a:Maintain your speed and lane as long as you don't cross the shoulder.,b:Drive to the right and stop immediately regardless of traffic.,c:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes away from the stopped vehicle; if a lane change is not safe, slow down and pass with extra space.
note: When passing a stopped emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, move over a lane if possible; otherwise slow down and provide extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, after coming to a complete stop you should first do what?
options: a:Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.,b:Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.,c:Look left
note: After stopping, scan left, then right, then left again to ensure the intersection is clear before proceeding.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Look in your rearview and side mirrors and check over your shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
note: Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: On slippery roads, how should you negotiate turns?
options: a:Reduce speed and take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly to avoid puddles.,c:Accelerate through the turn to maintain momentum.
note: Approach and negotiate curves at reduced speeds on slippery surfaces to maintain traction and control.

question: Which is a possible penalty for a first conviction of driving under the influence of alcohol?
options: a:Be required to drive with a restricted occupational license.,b:Lose your license for up to five years.,c:Be required to conduct a public education class on the dangers of drunk driving.
note: Penalties for a first DUI include fines and possible license suspension; more severe penalties depend on BAC and other factors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with care.,b:Continue normally through the intersection.,c:Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
note: A flashing yellow light means caution: slow down, look, and proceed carefully when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue driving,c:Slow to a stop
note: A steady yellow indicates the signal will change to red; slow and stop unless it is unsafe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make a quick lane change and turn from your lane of travel.,b:Back up on the shoulder to return to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit or other safe location to turn around.
note: Do not stop or back up on a freeway; proceed to the next exit and turn around where safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving on a two-lane street and a fire engine that is not using its emergency signals is following you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance from the engine.,b:Continue driving normally; you do not need to yield unless its lights or siren are on.,c:Pull immediately to the side and stop.
note: If the emergency vehicle has no lights or siren, you may continue in a normal manner; only clear the way when they are using signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes into a solid green light, what must you do before turning?
options: a:May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.,b:May no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:Still have the right-of-way to turn.
note: A green arrow gives protected movement; when it ends, you may turn on a green light but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must come to a complete stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A yellow arrow.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, then proceed when safe.

question: Which of the following penalties may be required for driving under the influence?
options: a:A $100 fine only.,b:No penalties for a first offense.,c:Attendance at Alcohol Highway Safety School.
note: First or second DUI offenses generally include, among other penalties, required attendance at Alcohol Highway Safety School.

question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Increase your speed to complete the turn faster.,b:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Activate your turn signal several seconds in advance.
note: Signal three to four seconds before turning to warn other road users of your intent.

question: How should you scan the road ahead to prepare for hazards?
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Continually scan the entire road and both roadsides.
note: Effective hazard detection requires continuously scanning the roadway and roadside areas, not staring fixedly or using improper foot position.

question: If someone under 16 uses a false ID to obtain alcohol, what happens to their driving privilege?
options: a:They will be barred from driving until age 21.,b:No action affects their license until they turn 21.,c:Their driving privilege will be suspended; if under 16, it begins when they turn 16.
note: If convicted while under 16 for possessing or obtaining alcohol via false ID, the driving suspension takes effect when the person turns 16.

question: If the center of the road has a broken yellow line, what does that tell you about the road?
options: a:You are on a one-way road.,b:The road is under repair.,c:You are on a two-way road (traffic moves in both directions).
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and may be crossed to pass when safe.

question: If arrested and a police officer requires you to take a blood, breath, or urine test, what is the legal consequence of refusing?
options: a:Your driving privilege will be automatically suspended for one year.,b:You may choose which test to take.,c:You will not face administrative suspension if later found not guilty.
note: Refusing a required chemical test leads to an automatic one-year license suspension under Pennsylvania's implied consent laws.

question: What does flashing red at a railroad crossing require you to do?
options: a:Stop. Do not proceed until signals are deactivated.,b:Slow down and proceed if the tracks are clear.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: Flashing red lights at railroad crossings warn of an approaching train; stop and remain stopped until signals are off and it is safe.

question: When you hear a fire engine or emergency vehicle approaching from behind, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with sirens or flashing lights, you must drive to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and lane changes are forbidden.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and permits lane changes when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross these lines?
options: a:To pass slower vehicles if the road is clear.,b:Only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, side road, or U-turn where permitted.,c:Never under any circumstance.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; crossing is allowed only for turning into driveways, alleys, or private roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum posted speed limit in this state?
note: Pennsylvania's maximum posted speed limit is 70 miles per hour on designated highways.

question: At a school crossing sign, what is the correct driver behavior?
options: a:Sound your horn when you see children near the road.,b:Always stop regardless of children being present.,c:Watch carefully for children and be ready to stop.
note: Be alert near school crossings and be prepared to stop for children, even if you don't see them right away.

question: At a light rail or train track crossing, what two actions are always required?
options: a:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Look both ways before crossing and obey signals and signs.,c:Pay attention and obey speed limit only.
note: Always look both directions before crossing tracks and obey all crossing signals and signs; never drive around lowered gates.

question: Where are road surfaces most likely to freeze quickly in cold weather?
options: a:Open sunny sections of road.,b:Shaded areas such as sections under trees or next to buildings.,c:Only steep
note: Shaded areas often freeze before sun-exposed parts and are the last to dry, so exercise extra caution there.

question: When parking facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,b:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, which of the following occurs?
options: a:Your reaction times slow and you make more driving errors.,b:You become more cautious and less likely to speed.,c:Metabolism speeds up and clears alcohol faster.
note: Alcohol slows reactions, impairs judgment, and increases the likelihood of mistakes while driving.

question: What does it mean when the solid white edge line angles toward the center of the road?
options: a:You will be required to turn left just ahead.,b:There is an intersection just ahead.,c:The roadway narrows ahead.
note: An edge line that angles inward signals that the roadway becomes narrower ahead; it marks the travel lane edge and shoulder.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster on wet roads.,b:Slow down and drive at a safe speed.,c:Drive through deep water to clear tires.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet surfaces; reducing speed helps tires maintain contact with the road.

question: Which of the following is illegal for anyone under 21 regarding alcohol?
options: a:Buy or consume alcohol.,b:Stand near someone who is drinking.,c:Wear clothing advertising alcohol.
note: It is unlawful for persons under 21 to buy or consume alcohol, and there are also restrictions on possession and transport.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal at an intersection is not working, how should you proceed?
options: a:Drive through cautiously without stopping.,b:Wait until a police officer arrives to direct traffic.,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
note: When traffic lights are out or malfunctioning, treat the intersection the same as a four-way stop: stop, yield as required, and proceed when safe.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:When passing another car on the highway just for courtesy.,b:To alert others if you lose control or to avoid a collision.,c:To express frustration at slow drivers.
note: Use your horn to warn others of imminent danger or loss of control—not for anger or routine passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane road, how should you react to merging traffic entering from an on-ramp?
options: a:Always speed up to pass the merging vehicle.,b:Make room for the entering vehicles by changing lanes if safe.,c:Maintain your speed and force them to merge behind you.
note: When space allows, change lanes to make room for merging vehicles so they can safely enter the traffic flow.

question: How does the type of alcoholic beverage affect impairment?
options: a:Is most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.,b:Is less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.,c:The effect on reflexes and judgment depends on total alcohol, not whether you drink beer, wine, or liquor.
note: All alcoholic beverages have the same effect on the body per unit of alcohol; impairment depends on the amount consumed, not the type.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a freeway, how should you look for a gap in traffic?
options: a:Looking in the inside rearview mirror only.,b:Looking in the side view mirror only.,c:Looking in both the rearview and side view mirrors and over your shoulder.
note: When merging, check all mirrors and look over your shoulder to find a safe gap in traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper procedure when merging onto a freeway?
options: a:Assume freeway traffic will slow for you and merge at any speed.,b:Enter slowly and stop if necessary before merging.,c:Use the acceleration lane to build speed, signal, and yield to freeway traffic, merging at a speed similar to the flow.
note: Use the acceleration lane to build speed, signal, and yield to freeway traffic while merging at similar speed to flow with traffic.

question: When a stopped school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, what must drivers do?
options: a:Only stop if you are behind the bus.,b:Pass cautiously if no children are visible.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and children are in a safe place.
note: Remain stopped for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm until the bus indicates it is safe to proceed.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the recommended immediate action?
options: a:Speed up to reach the nearest service station quickly.,b:Brake hard immediately and steer sharply to correct the skid.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and let the vehicle slow before pulling off the road.
note: Stay controlled: reduce speed gradually without heavy braking, maintain steering, and pull over safely.

question: What does the Four-second rule refer to?
options: a:Turn at stop signs.,b:Following another car.,c:Yield to other cars.
note: The Four-second rule is a guideline for maintaining a safe following distance on dry roads to allow time to react and stop.

question: If you cannot see cross traffic clearly while stopped at a stop sign, what should you do?
options: a:Creep forward slowly past the stop line until you can see, then proceed when safe.,b:Wait five seconds and then go even if you still cannot see.,c:Sound your horn and go without moving forward.
note: Carefully pull forward beyond the stop line to improve visibility, then check for traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

question: If you discover a defect that may affect safe operation of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.,c:Correct the defect only when you can afford it.
note: Any defect affecting safe operation should be repaired as soon as possible and before driving whenever feasible.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness on wet roadways as speed increases?
options: a:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective at gripping wet roads.
note: Higher speeds reduce the tires' ability to displace water, increasing the risk of hydroplaning and loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign that reads 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' means what about the new speed limit?
options: a:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,b:That you have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced zone.,c:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.
note: A posted reduced speed sign establishes the new speed limit beginning at that sign unless otherwise indicated.

question: If an emergency vehicle is using lights or siren and approaching, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers.,c:Pull to the right and slow down.
note: You must promptly drive to the right side of the road and stop when approached by an emergency vehicle using its warning devices.

question: After a train has passed, what should you do before proceeding across the tracks?
options: a:Immediately drive across if the first train is gone.,b:Wait for a green signal before crossing.,c:Look and listen again for another approaching train before crossing.
note: Even if one train has passed, check for other trains on adjacent tracks before you cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who does the law automatically give the right-of-way to at intersections?
options: a:No one.,b:Drivers going straight.,c:Drivers turning left.
note: The law does not grant automatic right-of-way to anyone; it specifies who must yield, but no one is inherently given it.

question: If a truck wants to pass you, how should you respond?
options: a:Your speed should remain steady or decrease.,b:You should change lanes.,c:You should stop.
note: When a large truck is passing, reduce speed slightly and maintain a steady reduced speed to help the truck pass safely.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up and leave the area immediately.,b:Turn on your hazard flashers and continue at the same speed.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: On a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren.

question: Which action best lowers your chance of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Replace tires that have bad tread.,b:Do not speed when the roads are wet.,c:Use tires with proper air pressure.
note: Hydroplaning is most often caused by excessive speed on wet roads; properly inflated tires and good tread also reduce the risk.

question: Is parental consent required for police to perform breath, blood, or urine tests on an underage arrestee?
options: a:Only required if the driver is under 16.,b:Yes; at least one parent must consent.,c:No; under implied consent, tests may be given without parental consent, though parents are notified.
note: Police may conduct chemical tests on underage arrestees without parental consent, but parents are notified of the arrest.

question: What do your brake lights indicate to other drivers?
options: a:You are making a turn.,b:You have your emergency brake on.,c:You are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights signal to drivers behind you that you are decelerating or stopping; keep them in working order.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn through the median.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.,c:Go to the next exit.
note: Do not stop, back up, or cross the median; continue to the next exit and re-route from there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal changes from green to yellow as you near an intersection, what is the best action?
options: a:Brake sharply to stop immediately in the intersection.,b:Speed up to get through before it turns red.,c:Be prepared to stop and do so if it is safe to stop before the intersection.
note: A yellow light means the signal will turn red; slow and stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,b:Once you see a toll booth.,c:On the main road
note: Move into the exit lane in advance and then slow down after you are in the exit lane to avoid impeding traffic on the main road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the yellow lights are flashing on a school zone speed sign, what is the speed limit?
note: When the school zone flashing lights are active or during posted school times, the maximum speed is 15 mph.

question: If a police officer stops you, what is the recommended behavior while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and open the window halfway.,b:Get your paperwork out immediately and reach for it as the officer approaches.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for instructions.
note: Remain seated with hands in view, ask passengers to do likewise, and wait until the officer requests documentation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes or passing on an interstate, what steps should you take first?
options: a:Apply the brake and change lanes quickly.,b:Assume other drivers will make room for you without signaling.,c:Signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and change lanes when safe.
note: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors and blind spot to ensure it is safe.

question: At night, which is the hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are the most difficult to see at night compared with signs or other vehicles.

question: If you must travel slower than 40 mph on a limited-access highway, you should:
options: a:Drive on the shoulder.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Use your hazard (four-way) flashers to warn drivers behind you.
note: When driving unusually slowly on a limited-access highway, use your four-way flashers to alert following drivers.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement onto the shoulder, what is the correct recovery method?
options: a:Slow down gradually, keep control, and steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Slam on your brakes and stop.,c:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
note: Keep control, slow down gently, and when safe steer back onto the pavement gradually; do not make sudden turns or braking maneuvers.

question: When you are in a line of traffic approaching a railroad crossing with no signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,b:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.,c:You have space to get all the way across the tracks without stopping.
note: Make sure there is room for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks before driving onto them; never pass another vehicle on a crossing approach.

question: What does an orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle mean?
options: a:The vehicle carries hazardous radioactive materials.,b:The vehicle will take wide turns.,c:The vehicle travels slower than normal traffic (25 mph or less).
note: An orange triangular emblem denotes a slow-moving vehicle, like farm equipment, that typically travels 25 mph or less.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
note: You should never use cruise control on snow, ice, or other hazardous conditions; winter demands extra caution and vehicle preparation.

question: For drivers under 21, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) are they considered driving under the influence in Pennsylvania?
options: a:0.02 percent or greater.,b:0.08 percent or greater.,c:0.05 percent or greater.
note: Pennsylvania enforces a zero-tolerance standard for under-21 drivers: a BAC of 0.02% or higher can lead to DUI penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: Driving so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow can be illegal and create hazards.

question: When roads are wet, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Drive the speed limit.,b:Drive slightly faster than the speed limit.,c:Reduce your speed by five to ten miles per hour.
note: Reduce your speed by approximately 5–10 mph in wet conditions, depending on how slippery the road is.

question: If another car appears likely to hit you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Use your emergency lights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians when you think they may not see you and a collision is possible.

question: What must drivers do when approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Continue driving if on opposite side of a divided highway where stopping is not required.,b:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed when required by law.
note: When a school bus is using its stop signal, drivers must stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn and children are clear.

question: What factors determine how much space you need to cross traffic safely?
options: a:Road and weather conditions, your vehicle’s acceleration, and speed/amount of oncoming traffic.,b:Only the presence of a stop sign ahead.,c:Whether you used your turn signals.
note: Space needed to cross traffic depends on road and weather conditions and the speed and volume of oncoming vehicles.

question: Which line marks the right edge of the roadway?
options: a:Broken white.,b:Solid yellow.,c:Solid white.
note: A solid white line is typically used to mark the right edge of the roadway, separating the travel lane from the shoulder.

question: What should you do to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Communicate with other road users.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads.
note: Use signals, horn, and eye contact when appropriate to communicate your intentions to drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do regarding oncoming traffic?
options: a:Swing to the right side of your lane to widen the turn.,b:Always sound your horn before turning.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing the turn.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when making a left turn to avoid collisions.

question: What should you remember when sharing the road with large trucks?
options: a:Trucks have a smaller turning radius than cars.,b:Trucks can stop quicker than cars on downgrades.,c:Trucks require longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles.
note: Due to their mass, large trucks need more distance to stop; allow them extra space on the road.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest overall practice regarding your speed relative to the flow of traffic?
options: a:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic (within the posted speed limit).
note: It is safest to travel with the general flow of traffic while obeying speed limits and adjusting for road conditions.

question: Which lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Red,b:White,c:Yellow
note: White lines divide lanes travelling in the same direction; broken white lines indicate lanes where passing is permitted.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed normally; pedestrian yields.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Take the right-of-way since vehicles are faster.
note: A white cane or guide dog signals a blind pedestrian; yield fully and be ready to stop to prevent injury.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: Immediately pull to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect you?
options: a:Do not affect driving abilities.,b:Are distracting activities.,c:Help maintain driver alertness.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you by taking your hands and eyes off the driving task, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and check mirrors only.,b:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
note: Always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot in the direction you plan to move before changing lanes.

question: Which type of crash is most common for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania?
options: a:Single-vehicle run-off-the-road crashes.,b:Rear-end collisions on interstates.,c:Parking-lot collisions.
note: The most frequent crash type involving 16-year-old drivers is a single-vehicle, run-off-the-road crash.

question: Before starting the engine, what should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure all passengers are buckled.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
note: Make a habit of buckling your safety belt and ensuring all passengers are buckled before switching on the ignition.

question: Which of the following is prohibited for anyone under 21 regarding alcohol?
options: a:Be in the presence of,b:Wear clothing advertising,c:Serve
note: Pennsylvania law prohibits certain alcohol-related activities for those under 21; convictions for alcohol offenses can affect driving privileges.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are used to mark no passing zones; some signs also include text to confirm this.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, what responsibility does a driver have?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them.,b:Only yield if the pedestrian is legally entitled to cross.,c:Require the pedestrian to make eye contact before yielding.
note: Drivers must be alert to pedestrians and yield to them to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you prepare to make a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:Close to the right side of the street.
note: When turning right you should position your vehicle as far to the right as practicable without leaving the roadway.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers should account for what truck characteristic?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The fact that trucks can stop in shorter distances than cars.,c:That trucks are quieter and thus easier to approach closely.
note: Other road users should allow for trucks' longer stopping distances and avoid lingering in blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must motorists do?
options: a:Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing despite the crossing guard's instructions.,c:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
note: Drivers must obey crossing guards and follow their instructions; reduce speed and use extra caution in school zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and a vehicle to your right arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and get through the intersection.,b:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,c:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and not dimming them, where should you look?
options: a:Either side,b:The center,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: When faced with an oncoming vehicle's high beams, glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while still keeping the road in view.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Open a window and drive on,b:Stop driving and rest or find a safe place to sleep.,c:Drink coffee and continue driving without stopping.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; the safest option is to stop and rest rather than continue driving drowsy.

question: If you must park on the roadway temporarily, what should you do to warn other drivers?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers and make sure your vehicle is visible for at least 500 feet.,b:Keep your turn signal on continuously.,c:Park at an angle to the flow of traffic.
note: Use hazard flashers and position your vehicle so other drivers can see it from a distance when parked on the roadway.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The time of day.,b:The condition of the road.,c:Signal lights.
note: Road conditions (wet, icy, gravel, etc.) strongly affect braking distance and control; reduce speed when conditions are poor.

question: What color background and lettering do highway and expressway guide signs typically have?
options: a:Yellow background with black letters.,b:Orange background with black letters.,c:Green background with white letters.
note: Guide signs on highways and expressways are generally green with white lettering to provide directional information.

question: When driving in rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain so your lights do not reflect excessively off the water and blind other drivers.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid to the left, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate.,b:Steer left.,c:Hit your brakes.
note: If the rear skids left, steer left (in the direction you want to go) to regain control; avoid braking hard or accelerating suddenly.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel slightly to avoid an obstacle.,b:Adjust the radio briefly while driving.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.
note: Distractions that divert your eyes, hands, or attention from driving increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers react to a steady yellow arrow signal?
options: a:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected turning time is ending; stop if you can do so safely.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their high beams, where should you glance to avoid being blinded?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right side of the road and down to avoid being blinded while retaining enough vision to stay on course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Use the shoulder.,b:Not cross the centerline.,c:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass when it is safe.
note: Passing on a two-lane road requires entering the oncoming traffic lane; only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,b:Only yield to traffic on the right.,c:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in the roadway.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow and yield to others already in the intersection or road, stopping if necessary.

question: If a truck appears to swing left before making a right turn, why is it dangerous to try to pass between the truck and the curb?
options: a:It is always safe because trucks give way to smaller vehicles.,b:Truck drivers may need the extra room and cannot see vehicles trying to squeeze by.,c:Large trucks always complete turns quickly without encroaching on the curb.
note: Trucks often require wide turning space and have large blind spots; attempting to pass between them and the curb is hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How soon before a turn should you activate your turn signal?
options: a:Only if there are vehicles behind you.,b:Three to four seconds before you reach the intersection.,c:Just as the front of your car reaches the intersection.
note: Signal three to four seconds in advance so others know your intent to turn or change lanes.

question: On wet roads, what following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Increase your following distance to five or six seconds.,b:Not be concerned about your following distance.,c:Decrease your following distance to two seconds.
note: Increase following distance to five or six seconds in wet conditions to allow extra stopping time.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Are passing a bicyclist.,b:Are traveling through an intersection.,c:See a child who is about to run into the street.
note: The horn should be used as a warning to others in immediate danger, such as a child about to run into the street.

question: What is the first thing you should adjust when getting into a car to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror.,b:Your seat belt.,c:Your seat.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach controls and see the road; then adjust mirrors and fasten your safety belt.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Directions to cities and towns.,b:Warning of conditions on or near the roadway ahead.,c:Traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped signs with a yellow background provide warnings about road conditions or hazards ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.,c:Slow and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed with caution.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will turn red soon; stop safely if you can, otherwise clear the intersection.

question: If you are under 21 and convicted of driving under the influence, what is the length of the license suspension for a first offense under Pennsylvania law?
options: a:30-day suspension.,b:Six-month suspension.,c:12-month suspension.
note: Drivers under 21 face a 12-month license suspension for a DUI first offense under the high-rate penalty provisions.

question: What is the effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:It causes no measurable driving errors.,b:It distracts you and makes it difficult to stay in your lane and control the vehicle.,c:It makes you a more alert driver by preventing hunger.
note: Handling food or drink while driving takes hands and eyes off the road, increasing the risk of errors and lane deviations.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle, front, rear, and both sides.,b:Only in front of your vehicle.,c:Only behind your vehicle.
note: Maintain space around your vehicle on all sides to allow time and room to react to hazards.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
note: When there are no lights or gates, be prepared to yield to trains and do not cross until you can clear the tracks and it is safe.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you pass the bicyclist?
options: a:Squeeze between both hazards to maintain speed.,b:Move to the shoulder to pass both at once.,c:Allow the oncoming car to pass first
note: Deal with one hazard at a time: wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass, then pass the bicyclist with adequate space.

question: Which color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines divide lanes moving the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.,b:The car in which the driver sounds his horn first has the right-of-way.,c:The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.
note: At an intersection of roads with no traffic control, drivers must yield to vehicles approaching from the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:Turning left or right.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder whenever you change your vehicle's position, especially when changing lanes.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Wear your seat belt.,c:Limit your driving to weekdays.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce the likelihood of injury or death in a crash.

question: If your vehicle turn signals are not working, what alternate method should you use to show turning intentions?
options: a:Your headlights.,b:Your horn.,c:Hand signals.
note: Use standard hand signals to indicate turns when mechanical turn signals fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there are no signs, signals, or police at an intersection, who must yield?
options: a:Drivers on the right must yield to drivers on the left.,b:Drivers turning left must yield to vehicles going straight.,c:There are no laws about who must yield.
note: When no controls are present, drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, how should you react?
options: a:No special action is required.,b:The driver should honk their horn.,c:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.
note: Be cautious and pass animals slowly to avoid startling them and causing unpredictable movement into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the light is green but oncoming traffic is heavy and you want to turn left, you should:
options: a:Wait behind the crosswalk until traffic clears.,b:Use the next intersection.,c:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
note: You may enter the intersection to prepare for a left turn on a green light, but only if it is safe and you will not block traffic; otherwise delay your turn.

question: If a railroad crossing has no signals, what should you do as you approach?
options: a:Proceed as quickly as possible over the tracks.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if you see or hear a train approaching.,c:Proceed through the crossing at a normal rate.
note: When crossing where no active warnings exist, slow down and be ready to stop if you see or hear a train approaching.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what should you do regarding lane usage?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle when possible.,b:Allow the motorcycle to share half your lane.,c:Give the motorcycle the full width of a lane as it is a full-size vehicle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; never try to share a lane or crowd a motorcyclist.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling the same direction as you?
options: a:Continue driving straight; it is the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of your way.,b:Do not pass the bicyclist until you come to a traffic signal or stop sign.,c:Slow down and wait until there is no traffic approaching in the opposite lane, then change lanes (or give at least 3–4 feet of clearance) and pass safely.
note: Pass bicyclists only when it is safe, leaving at least 3 to 4 feet of clearance (more at higher speeds) and not passing too fast or close.

question: Why is night driving generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Roads are always more slippery at night.,b:Cars overheat more at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark
note: Reduced visibility at night requires lower speeds, proper headlights, and greater caution.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beams.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low-beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped); high beams can reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

question: On a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
note: On narrow roads, you must leave at least half of the main-traveled portion for oncoming traffic so both vehicles can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you turn left on a red light?
options: a:You are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.,b:There is no traffic coming from the opposite direction.,c:You are turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
note: You may turn left on red only from the left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street after stopping and yielding, unless prohibited by sign.

question: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass cautiously if no children are visible.,b:Pass the bus if you are on the opposite side of any road.,c:Stop at least 10 feet away and remain stopped until lights are off and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm, staying at least 10 feet away until it's safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A steady green arrow gives protected turning movement and the right-of-way to turn in the arrow's direction.

question: How can stress influence your driving performance?
options: a:It helps you react faster in emergencies.,b:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and increase driving errors.,c:It makes you less likely to be in an accident.
note: Strong emotions and stress reduce concentration, perception, and judgment, which can impair driving ability.

question: What should you do on slippery roads to reduce collision risk?
options: a:Use alternate routes.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: On slippery roads increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead because stopping distances are longer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving speed is true?
options: a:Driving at the posted speed limit is always the safest.,b:Driving slower is always safest regardless of conditions.,c:The safest driving speed depends on many conditions
note: A safe speed depends on conditions like visibility, road surface, and traffic flow; sometimes you must drive below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where signals are working, whose directions should you follow?
options: a:Wait for a signal from another driver.,b:Obey the traffic signal and ignore the officer.,c:Follow the officer’s directions rather than the traffic lights.
note: An officer’s directions take precedence over traffic signals; always follow the officer’s instructions for safety and legal compliance.

question: After an emergency vehicle with siren and lights has passed you, how far should you remain behind it?
options: a:Follow closely to provide help if needed.,b:Remain directly behind it to form a convoy.,c:Stay well behind it, about 500 feet or as your state law requires.
note: You must not drive closer than 500 feet behind an emergency vehicle that is responding to a call.

question: What is the most important speed-management rule on curves?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed limit when entering the curve and then brake later.,b:Accelerate into the curve to maintain lane position.,c:Slow down before entering the curve so you can safely complete it.
note: Because of inertia, you should reduce speed before a curve to maintain control through it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means you may:
options: a:Must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Drive through or turn if allowed, after yielding.,c:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
note: A steady green light allows you to proceed through the intersection or make permitted turns, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

question: A red flashing traffic signal indicates what action?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,b:Yield to all traffic but do not stop.,c:Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe (same as a stop sign).
note: A flashing red means stop: treat the intersection as you would a stop sign and yield before proceeding.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red, how should you proceed?
options: a:Honk and proceed since you have the right-of-way.,b:Yield to the pedestrians and wait until they have crossed safely.,c:Speed up to pass in front of them quickly.
note: Yield to pedestrians even if they are crossing incorrectly; safety takes precedence over traffic signals in such situations.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing at an intersection without a traffic signal?
options: a:Whoever started moving last,b:The driver,c:Whoever is slower
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers entering a roundabout or traffic circle do?
options: a:Must always stop before entering.,b:Have the right-of-way if there is one lane.,c:Must yield to drivers already in the roundabout or traffic circle.
note: Vehicles entering a roundabout must yield to traffic already circulating in the circle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left toward the center of the road.,b:Keep your wheels straight ahead at all times.,c:Turn your wheels to the right so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.
note: Turn the front wheels toward the curb (right on a two-way street when parking downhill) to prevent rolling into traffic.

question: If arrested for DUI and you refuse to take a required chemical test, what administrative penalty follows?
options: a:An automatic driver license suspension.,b:A mandatory drug counseling course only.,c:A single day in jail without other penalties.
note: Refusing required chemical testing after DUI arrest results in an automatic license suspension under implied consent laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady green,b:Steady red,c:Flashing yellow
note: A steady yellow warns that a steady red will soon appear.

question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull alongside and argue to defend your position.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Move out of their way and avoid engaging or making eye contact.
note: Avoid escalation: yield space, avoid eye contact, and let the aggressive driver pass when safe.

question: If your blood alcohol concentration is 0.04 percent, how does your crash risk compare to someone with no alcohol?
options: a:Your crash risk is higher than with no alcohol.,b:You are below any increased risk and are safe to drive.,c:You are certain you will drive safely at that level.
note: Even a BAC of .04 significantly increases crash risk compared to having no alcohol in your system.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:The area you see in your rearview mirror.,b:Directly behind your vehicle.,c:The area you cannot see without moving your head.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot view using your mirrors and require a head check to see.

question: What is the minimum legal drinking age in Pennsylvania?
options: a:18 years old.,b:20 years old.,c:21 years old.
note: The minimum legal age to purchase and possess alcoholic beverages in Pennsylvania is 21.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Keep your normal speed and turn,b:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection before turning.,c:Stop first and then make the turn regardless of conditions.
note: Turning on a steady green is allowed unless prohibited, but you must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles with the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you continue carefully through an intersection displaying a yellow light?
options: a:If there is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.,b:If you are already within the intersection.,c:If there are pedestrians crossing.
note: If a steady yellow appears while you are already in the intersection, proceed through carefully; otherwise prepare to stop.

question: While backing, what is the safest technique?
options: a:Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.
note: When backing, turn your head and look out the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Go.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red; slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

question: When driving where children might play, what should you expect?
options: a:Children will always wait for traffic to clear.,b:Children will follow crosswalk rules reliably.,c:Children may run into the street without looking
note: Expect unpredictable actions from children near play areas and reduce speed to be ready to stop.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are required to step aside for vehicles.,b:They are likely blind and may need you to yield fully and be prepared to stop.,c:They are directing traffic.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates the pedestrian is blind; you must slow down, yield, and be ready to stop.

question: How many minutes does it take an average person to metabolize the alcohol from one standard drink?
note: An average person needs about one hour to process the alcohol in a single drink; factors such as weight and metabolism affect this.

question: If someone under 21 consumes alcohol but is not driving, the minimum penalty for a first offense is:
options: a:A six-month probation.,b:A 90-day driver license suspension and up to a $500 fine.,c:A sentence to a corrections institution.
note: Minimum penalties for a first underage drinking offense include up to a $500 fine plus a 90-day license suspension.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is always prohibited.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and permits passing when it is safe.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line adjacent to your lane means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: At highway speeds on a dry road, what is a safe minimum following distance?
options: a:Three seconds.,b:Two seconds.,c:Four seconds.
note: At higher speeds on dry pavement, a four-second following distance gives adequate time to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On two-lane, two-way streets, where should you begin a left turn?
options: a:As close to the centerline as possible.,b:From the far right side of your lane.,c:From the curb side of the lane.
note: Make left turns from the lane nearest the centerline, keeping close to the center to minimize encroachment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:Single broken yellow line.,b:Single solid white line.,c:Double solid yellow lines.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means no passing is permitted from either direction.

question: In foggy conditions, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low-beam headlights and fog lights if equipped in fog; high beams can worsen visibility by reflecting off the fog.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately locate the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,b:Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.,c:Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
note: If you hear an emergency vehicle nearby but can't see it, safely pull to the right and stop until you determine whether the vehicle is approaching your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Flash your headlights immediately before passing.,b:Signal in advance to indicate your intention to change lanes and pass.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers while passing.
note: Use your turn signal early enough to alert other drivers before you start to pass.

question: What should you remember about driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Roads are especially slippery just after rain begins due to oil and dirt on the surface.,b:Wet roads never affect stopping distance.,c:You can drive the same as on dry pavement if visibility is good.
note: Road surfaces can be most slippery right after rain starts; slow down and increase following distance.

question: Which of the following is recommended to drive safely at night?
options: a:Use high beams at all times to maximize visibility.,b:Drive only with parking lights on.,c:Increase your following distance so you can stop within the visible area.
note: At night reduce speed and increase following distance so you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.

question: How much sleep should teenagers try to get nightly to reduce crash risk from drowsy driving?
options: a:Eight hours,b:Seven hours,c:Six hours
note: Teenagers should aim for about eight hours of sleep per night to reduce the risk of drowsy driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,c:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway and yield to any approaching vehicles and pedestrians; stop before the sidewalk area.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs along with alcohol on driving safety?
options: a:Increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.,c:Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) intensifies impairment and increases crash risk.

question: How does fatigue affect driving ability compared to alcohol?
options: a:Being tired improves concentration compared to drinking.,b:Fatigue only slightly reduces driving ability compared to alcohol.,c:Lack of sleep can impair driving similar to having a measurable blood alcohol level.
note: Being awake 18 hours impairs driving similar to a .05 BAC; 24 hours awake is similar to about .10 BAC.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side and one train has passed, what must you do?
options: a:Cross immediately to beat any other approaching trains.,b:Look for a second train on the other track before crossing.,c:Assume it is safe to cross once the first train is gone.
note: When two tracks exist, another train may be approaching on the adjacent track; only cross when clear.

question: If a vehicle approaching you has high beams on, what is the safest immediate action?
options: a:Turn on your high beams to signal them.,b:Turn off your headlights completely.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road and avoid looking directly at the lights.
note: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, avert your gaze to the right roadway edge to avoid temporary blindness.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Anything makes conditions less than perfect.,b:You see a police car.,c:Entering a highway where there are other cars.
note: If visibility, traction, or other conditions are poor, reduce speed below the posted limit to maintain safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,b:Signal a lane change.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes you should signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: What is a 'No zone' in relation to large vehicles?
options: a:A designated no-passing zone on a highway.,b:The large blind spot around a truck where the driver cannot see you.,c:A one-way traffic area near heavy trucks.
note: 'No zones' are the large blind spots around big trucks; avoid lingering in these areas to stay visible to the truck driver.

question: What should you do when driving in fog?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:Drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: Use low beam headlights (or fog lights if equipped) in fog; high beams will cause glare and reduce visibility.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how does driving at night differ?
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:More dangerous.,c:Less dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because visibility is reduced, glare from headlights can blind you, and there tend to be more tired or impaired drivers on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, you should:
options: a:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.,b:Wait until you can see all of the lanes you need to cross before making the turn.,c:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.
note: Do not begin the left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and you can complete the turn safely.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use to be visible and safe?
options: a:Use your hazard flashers and, if needed, parking lights so others see you.,b:Turn off all your lights.,c:Use your parking lights only.
note: If stopped at night, use emergency flashers and keep low beams on so other road users can clearly see your vehicle.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what is a proper safety action?
options: a:Stay in the lane and wait for a tow to arrive.,b:Sound your horn to alert passing motorists.,c:Turn on your hazard flashers
note: Use hazard flashers, move off the roadway, and signal that your vehicle is disabled to protect yourself and others.

question: When do roads typically become especially slippery after rain begins?
options: a:The day after it rains.,b:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Pavement is most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of rain because oil rises to the surface; this effect can be worse in hot weather.

question: When parked uphill on a street with a curb, which action is correct?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
note: On an uphill park with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so a rollback will not move you into traffic.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' caused by?
options: a:Frequent rest stops that interrupt driving rhythm.,b:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning.,c:Getting too much sleep before the trip.
note: Highway hypnosis results from prolonged monotony and failure to actively scan the roadway, leading to zoning out.

question: If you are under 21 and convicted of carrying a false ID, what happens even if you were not driving?
options: a:Only if you were driving at the time of arrest.,b:Only if your blood alcohol content (BAC) is 0.02 percent or higher.,c:Even if you were not driving.
note: A conviction for possessing a false ID or unlawfully possessing alcohol can result in fines and suspension of driving privileges for under-21 drivers even if they were not driving.

question: When passing a bicyclist, what minimum clearance should you give?
options: a:Give them at least three feet of space.,b:Remain on the right side of your lane.,c:Blast your horn to alert the bicyclist.
note: State law requires allowing at least four feet between your vehicle and a bicyclist when passing; leave more room at higher speeds.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.,b:Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,c:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating and recognizing potential hazards and acting to avoid collisions before they occur.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when may you proceed?
options: a:Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.,b:Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.,c:Go through as soon as the train passes.
note: Do not proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks; another train may be approaching on a separate track.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, what is true about larger vehicles' blind spots?
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:No blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: Big vehicles like trucks have larger blind spots to their sides and rear; avoid lingering in these areas.

question: How does increasing speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your peripheral awareness.,b:It has no effect on vision,c:It decreases your field of vision
note: Higher speeds narrow your field of vision, reducing your ability to detect hazards off-center.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic fatalities in work zones?
options: a:Hydroplaning from sprayed water on the roadway.,b:Tire blowouts from construction materials.,c:Driver carelessness and speeding.
note: Most work-zone fatalities result from drivers' carelessness and speeding through the work area.

question: Drivers are at increased crash risk when using which device while driving?
options: a:Radio with preset controls.,b:CD player with automatic changer.,c:Cell phone (including hands-free).
note: Using a cell phone—hands-free included—distracts attention and increases crash risk significantly.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what must you do?
options: a:Look for a train.,b:Slow down and look for a train.,c:Stop and remain stopped until signals stop and tracks are clear.
note: When crossing signals are flashing you must stop no closer than 15 feet from the rail and wait until it is safe to proceed.

question: For drivers 21 and older in Pennsylvania, what BAC is illegal to operate a vehicle?
options: a:0.08 percent or higher.,b:0.05 percent or higher.,c:0.02 percent or higher.
note: It is illegal for drivers age 21+ to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or greater.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road, when may you pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the vehicle ahead is turning or signaling a left turn or when there are two or more marked lanes in your direction.,b:Never, under any circumstance.,c:Only on a single lane entrance ramp.
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left or when the roadway has multiple marked lanes going the same direction.

question: What typically causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Sudden turns that throw water under the tires.,b:Making frequent stops on wet roads.,c:Increasing speed which reduces tire ability to clear water.
note: When you drive too fast on wet pavement your tires may not clear water effectively and can ride on a film of water, causing the vehicle to slide—this is hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you turn right on a red light in Pennsylvania?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic unless a sign prohibits it.,b:If you are facing a red arrow pointing right.,c:From the left lane of a one-way street.
note: You may turn right on red after a full stop and yielding to others, unless a sign specifically prohibits it.

question: What should you do to your speed when making a turn?
options: a:Maintain your current speed throughout the turn.,b:Reduce your speed so you can maintain control and stay in your lane.,c:Increase speed to complete the turn quickly.
note: Slow to a speed that allows you to control the vehicle and respond to unexpected hazards while turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you normally do?
options: a:Always stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Enter slowly and stop if necessary before merging.,c:Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic
note: Acceleration lanes are provided so you can increase speed to match traffic before merging safely.

question: When should you allow a larger than usual space cushion in front of your vehicle while stopped?
options: a:At a stop sign.,b:At an intersection.,c:When stopped on an uphill slope.
note: Allow extra space when stopped on an uphill slope so if the vehicle ahead rolls backward you have room to avoid a collision.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:Bad driving habit.,b:Unnecessary action.,c:Good driving habit.
note: Glancing over your shoulder to check blind spots is a crucial and safe driving practice when changing lanes or merging.

question: If you must slow or stop where other drivers might not expect it, what should you do first?
options: a:Look over your shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.,b:Use your emergency brake.,c:Quickly tap your brake pedal a few times first.
note: If you need to stop unexpectedly, tap the brake pedal several times to warn following drivers and activate the brake lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure?
options: a:The passing lane is clear and you signal before changing lanes.,b:You may only pass on the right regardless of conditions.,c:That oncoming traffic yields to you.
note: Confirm the lane is clear, signal in advance, and change lanes only when it is safe to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who should proceed first?
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:One driver should continue driving without stopping.
note: At four-way stops the first vehicle to arrive goes first; if two arrive together, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

question: Teen drivers have a higher crash risk when they are driving with which passengers?
options: a:Other teenage passengers.,b:Adult passengers.,c:Pets as passengers.
note: Crash risk increases for teen drivers when other teenagers are present as passengers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn from a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left lane.,c:The center lane.
note: When turning left from a one-way street with multiple lanes, begin the turn from the leftmost lane.

question: After an accident that leaves your vehicle blocking traffic, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait until the police arrive before moving your vehicle.,b:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,c:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
note: After a minor collision, move vehicles out of traffic if it is safe to do so, but do not leave the scene without identifying yourself and offering assistance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best thing to do when you become sleepy while driving?
options: a: Increase your speed to get away from other vehicles,b: Move over to the right lane and continue driving,c: Drive to a safe place stop and rest
note: When you start to feel sleepy while driving, your reaction time, judgment, and awareness drop quickly, and rolling down a window or turning up the radio will not keep you safe. The safest action is to get off the road as soon as you can safely do so, park in a safe place, and rest before continuing to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Medications for sleep, anxiety, pain, colds, or allergies.
options: a: May impair your driving,b: May increase the bad effects of alcohol on your driving,c: Both of the above
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, including those for sleep, anxiety, pain, colds, or allergies, can make you drowsy, dizzy, or less alert, which impairs driving. When combined with alcohol, these effects can become much stronger and more dangerous, greatly increasing your risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You shouldn’t drive.
options: a: After you have taken any drink drug or medication which changes how you think or act or causes you to be less careful,b: If you are not alert,c: Both of the above
